strengths: Clear problem identification and well-motivated solution combining compact initialization (16× subsampled space) with recurrent refinement via rendering error feedback
Strong and comprehensive experimental validation across multiple settings (8/16 views, multiple resolutions, DL3DV and RealEstate10K), with proper comparisons to re-trained baselines
Insightful use of rendering error as naturally adaptive feedback signal enabling superior generalization to unseen datasets and resolutions compared to single-step methods
Significant practical benefits: 16× Gaussian reduction with maintained/improved quality, 100× speedup over 3DGS optimization, 2.7 dB PSNR improvement over DepthSplat on DL3DV
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (kNN attention, global attention, rendering error, ResNet features)
Honest discussion of limitations and commitment to code release for reproducibility
State-of-the-art results on multiple benchmarks while using substantially fewer Gaussians than competing methods
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily an effective combination of standard techniques (depth prediction, point clouds, kNN/global attention) rather than novel methodological contributions
Reconstruction time slower than key baseline Long-LRM (0.7-1.7s vs 0.4s on DL3DV 16-view), undermining efficiency claims; limited profiling or optimization analysis provided
Convergence plateau at 3 iterations not well understood—no analysis of why rendering errors remain but updates stop; authors speculate fixed Gaussian count but provide no evidence
Generalization evaluated only on similar indoor/building domains (DL3DV, RealEstate10K); lacks evaluation on diverse out-of-distribution scenarios (synthetic, outdoor, different cameras)

16× compression factor trade-off under-explored: Table 4 shows 1.6 dB loss vs 4× compression; ablations conducted only at low resolution (256×448), not at full resolution (512×960) where compression matters
Scalability concerns remain fundamental: kNN bottleneck acknowledged at >500K Gaussians; 16× subsampling was partly motivated by this, creating circular reasoning about efficiency
Missing comparisons with SplatFormer on scene-level benchmarks and limited analysis comparing rendering-error feedback vs. explicit gradient-based refinement methods
Two-stage training necessity not justified—no ablation comparing joint end-to-end training; theoretical motivation for freezing initial model unclear
Technical details under-specified: rendering error propagation mechanism could be formalized; ResNet-18 choice lacks justification; hyperparameter choices (α, λ, γ, k) not sensitivity-analyzed
Terminology slightly misleading: 'gradient-free' updates still require computing rendering, just without backpropagation through Gaussian optimization

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (DL3DV, RealEstate10K), resolutions (256×256 to 540×960), and view counts (2, 8, 16), with particularly valuable cross-dataset and cross-resolution generalization studies.
Practical contribution addressing real limitation of single-pass feed-forward methods through a gradient-free recurrent mechanism guided by rendering error feedback.
Significant reduction in Gaussian count (16×) compared to per-pixel methods, yielding 4× faster rendering speed while improving quality.
Solid experimental results: +2.7 dB PSNR over DepthSplat on DL3DV 8-view, outperforms Long-LRM at 16-view with 4× fewer Gaussians, state-of-the-art on RealEstate10K among feed-forward 3DGS models.
Well-designed ablation studies (Table 5) validating importance of rendering error feedback and attention mechanisms.
Clear presentation and commitment to reproducibility (promised code release, pre-trained models).
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Recurrent refinement with error feedback is established in learned optimization literature; rendering error as feedback is intuitive but incremental. Heavy reliance on DepthSplat architecture limits conceptual contribution.

Misleading efficiency claims: '100× faster than 3DGS' compares against per-scene optimization (fundamentally different use case), not fair-comparison feed-forward baselines. ReSplat reconstruction time at 3 iterations (0.693s) is 3.6× slower than DepthSplat (0.190s) on same hardware—this cost-benefit analysis is inadequately discussed.

Rapid convergence plateau: Model saturates after only 3 iterations (0→1 iter: +0.48 dB; 1→2: +0.11 dB; 2→3: +0.02 dB diminishing returns). Speculation about fixed Gaussians limiting iterations lacks investigation. Questions whether recurrent mechanism is necessary given modest accumulated gain (~0.6 dB PSNR).

Incomplete computational analysis: kNN attention acknowledged as expensive for >500K points, limiting scalability. No wall-clock time per quality-improvement analysis. Complex two-stage training with progressive resolution schedule sensitivity unexplored.

Unfair baseline comparisons: 3DGS comparison uses 4K iterations without evidence this is convergence; paper claims longer optimization causes overfitting but provides no empirical support. Long-LRM comparison on 16-view borrows published results rather than controlled retraining.

Test-time advantage not clearly acknowledged: Method requires ground-truth input views at test time for rendering error computation—inapplicable to scenarios lacking input view ground truth, yet this constraint is not prominently discussed as a limitation.

Limited technical depth on feedback mechanism: No visualization/analysis of what network learns from rendering error or which scene regions are refined. Ablation removes error entirely but offers no intermediate analysis. No exploration of alternative feedback signals.

Generalization experiments scope is narrow: Only DL3DV→RealEstate10K tested; RealEstate10K acknowledged as 'easier'; cross-resolution results show only downsampling from training resolution; no substantially different scene type transfers (e.g., outdoor→indoor).

Arbitrary hyperparameter choices with insufficient justification: 16× compression described as 'good trade-off' without principled selection method (Table 4 shows 24.77→28.36 PSNR range). ResNet-18 feature extraction specifics (1/2, 1/4, 1/8 resolutions) unexplored. Exponential weighting γ=0.9 unjustified.

Statistical rigor absent: No error bars, confidence intervals, or variance across scenes. Unclear if sub-dB improvements are statistically significant. Table 1 shows diminishing returns but frames as 'converges after 3 iterations' without deeper analysis.

Two-stage training complexity: Sensitivity to stage 1 initialization quality not explored. Progressive training schedule dependency not investigated. Makes reproducibility and generalization less transparent.

Incomplete comparison with related work: SplatFormer dismissed as object-centric without direct experimental comparison. Distinction via rendering error is noted but feels somewhat arbitrary since SplatFormer also refines predictions.

Unfair RealEstate10K setup: Different compression factor (4× vs 16×) and decoder configuration (4 Gaussians per point) than main experiments. Comparison with LVSM shows only 1.1 dB improvement but acknowledges 20× slower rendering—undermining efficiency narrative.

strengths: Elegant use of rendering error as feedback signal for gradient-free Gaussian updates that naturally enables test-time adaptation
Significant practical efficiency: 16× fewer Gaussians, 4× faster rendering than DepthSplat, 100× faster than 3DGS optimization
Strong experimental results: +3.3dB PSNR over 3DGS on DL3DV 8-view; 4× fewer Gaussians than Long-LRM with higher quality on 16-view setup
Excellent generalization validation: robust to unseen datasets (RealEstate10K) and resolutions (+4dB when adapting from 512×960 to 320×640)
Comprehensive ablation studies validating kNN attention, global attention, and rendering error components
Well-designed two-stage training strategy balancing efficiency and quality
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and thorough implementation details
Demonstrated reproducibility commitment with promised code and model release
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: primarily combines existing techniques (DepthSplat initialization, standard attention mechanisms); main novelty is the rendering error application which is somewhat incremental
Computational scalability issues not resolved: kNN attention expensive for >500K points; reconstruction slower than Long-LRM (0.7s vs 0.4s); acknowledged but unaddressed

Insufficient analysis of rendering error as feedback signal: lacks comparison to alternative feedback mechanisms or perceptual networks; no visualization of how error guides updates; weak theoretical justification for effectiveness
Training complexity: requires two-stage pipeline with progressive resolution increases across 3 stages; expensive (16 GH200 GPUs); adds development burden
Limited dataset diversity: only DL3DV and RealEstate10K evaluated; RealEstate10K at low resolution (256×256); no evaluation on other standard benchmarks (ScanNet, Matterport)
Convergence saturation at 3 iterations limits test-time compute flexibility and further improvements; fixed Gaussian count during recurrence may limit expressiveness
No failure case analysis: missing discussion of underperforming scenarios, challenging scene types, or applicability limitations
Inconsistent experimental setup on RealEstate10K: uses 4× subsampling (not 16×) producing per-pixel Gaussian counts, undermining compression advantage claims for this benchmark

strengths: Novel use of rendering error as gradient-free feedback signal to guide iterative Gaussian refinement, with clear motivation and effective execution
Significant practical efficiency gains: 16× reduction in Gaussians while maintaining quality, 4× faster rendering than comparable methods
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (DL3DV, RealEstate10K, ACID), input views (8/16/32), and resolutions, with strong generalization
Thorough ablation studies (Table 6) validating design choices including coordinate systems, compression factors, and architectural components
Strong empirical results with 4.2dB PSNR improvement over 3DGS optimization and consistent improvements across configurations
Technical soundness with well-formulated approach combining subsampled 3D space reconstruction, rendering error computation, and weight-sharing recurrent updates
Clear presentation with informative figures and detailed implementation details supporting reproducibility; promises code release
Practical contribution addressing real limitation of feed-forward Gaussian splatting in sparse-view scenarios
weaknesses: Incremental novelty in components: kNN attention, global attention, and depth smoothness losses are borrowed from existing work; main novelty is their combination and use of rendering error as feedback
Scalability limitations with kNN attention becoming computationally expensive for large numbers of Gaussians (>500K), limiting applicability to very large scenes

Limited comparison with some concurrent methods; comparison with SplatFormer noted as 'non-trivial to make work' but not thoroughly investigated; GS-LRM and LVSM mentioned but not comprehensively compared

Insufficient analysis of design choices: why middle-view COLMAP coordinate system works best (Table 6b) lacks explanation; what is learned at each iteration not analyzed; saturation at 4 iterations unexplained

Rendering error as feedback not rigorously compared against alternative feedback signals (photometric loss, depth consistency); choice appears empirically validated but lacks comparative justification
Compression factor selection (16×) analyzed empirically but lacks principled analysis of speedup-accuracy trade-offs across different scenarios
No analysis of failure cases or limitations; unclear how method performs with extreme lighting changes, heavy occlusions, reflective surfaces, or challenging appearance variations
Ablation study incompleteness: tests combined removal of kNN and global attention but not individual ablations to isolate their separate contributions
Lack of theoretical grounding for why recurrent approach should outperform single-step methods; intuitive motivation provided but formal analysis absent
Limited evaluation of generalization to very challenging scenes; mostly tested on relatively structured indoor/outdoor datasets; unclear behavior with extreme motion or appearance variation

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, view configurations, and resolutions with detailed ablation studies demonstrating the contribution of each component
Strong and consistent empirical results showing 27.70 PSNR on DL3DV (4.24dB over optimization-based 3DGS) with 4× fewer Gaussians and faster rendering than Long-LRM
Robust cross-dataset generalization to unseen scenes and resolutions without retraining, suggesting learned refinement strategy is generally applicable
Clear problem motivation and well-justified design choices for spatial compression and coordinate system selection, validated through systematic ablations (Table 6)
Reproducibility provisions including promised code release, detailed implementation information, and training procedures in appendix
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: the core contribution (iterative refinement using rendering error feedback) applies well-established practices to 3D Gaussian splatting with minimal methodological innovation

Incomplete baseline comparisons: SplatFormer (directly comparable concurrent work) is relegated to appendix with no main paper analysis; comparisons with single-step methods unfairly pit T=4 iterations against T=1
Modest quality gains over optimization-based baseline (only 0.93dB PSNR improvement over 3DGS optimization); primary value is speed rather than fundamentally better reconstruction
Scalability limitations acknowledged but not addressed: kNN-based attention becomes prohibitively expensive beyond ~5000K points; 16× compression is a workaround rather than principled solution

Insufficient failure case analysis and generalization claims: tested only on similar indoor datasets, no evaluation on diverse scene types (outdoor large-scale, highly structured/unstructured); generalization to very sparse views unexplored

Design choices lack principled justification: coordinate system choice is post-hoc empirical (Table 6b), no systematic comparison of rendering error vs. alternative feedback signals, hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored
Two-stage training complexity (freeze initialization model, train only recurrent refinement) lacks justification for why end-to-end training is infeasible
Insufficient analysis of learned representations: ablations show recurrent model matters but provide no insight into what patterns are learned across iterations or how Gaussian parameters evolve

Technical presentation issues: global attention mechanism (Eq. 6) introduced abruptly with unclear computational strategy; motivation for combining local (kNN) and global attention not well articulated
Limitations section is superficial (only ~150 words) with minimal discussion of when/why the method fails, fundamental scalability constraints, or impact on downstream applications

strengths: Well-motivated core insight: Using rendering error as iterative feedback for Gaussian refinement is intuitive, effective, and well-justified theoretically and empirically
Significant practical improvements: 100× speedup over 3DGS optimization, 4× faster rendering than per-pixel methods, with 16× Gaussian compression while maintaining/improving quality

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple datasets (DL3DV, RealEstate10K, ACID), varying configurations (2-32 views, 256×256 to 540×960 resolution), extensive ablations, and strong cross-dataset/cross-resolution generalization

Technically sound implementation with well-designed rendering error propagation combining pixel and feature-space signals, effective kNN attention for spatial compression, and empirically validated architectural choices
Strong reproducibility commitment with promised code/model release, clear mathematical formulation, detailed implementation, and results that enable community verification
Demonstrated robustness across diverse scenarios: generalizes to unseen datasets and configurations despite training only on DL3DV, important for practical deployment
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual technical components: Initial Gaussian prediction closely follows DepthSplat, and components like kNN attention and multi-scale features are established techniques; contribution is primarily in effective combination rather than fundamental innovation

Incomplete exploration of design space: Number of iterations (4) appears heuristic without principled stopping criterion; Gaussian compression factor (16×) lacks systematic exploration of alternatives (2-4-8×); trade-offs between speed and accuracy not thoroughly analyzed

Scalability constraints with kNN attention: Acknowledged limitation that kNN becomes prohibitive for very large Gaussian populations (500K+); no investigation of alternative efficient attention mechanisms; represents hard constraint on flexibility

Limited failure mode analysis: No systematic discussion of when rendering error feedback is misleading or insufficient; missing analysis of dataset/scene types where method struggles or confidence estimation for output quality

Experimental scope limitations: Main DL3DV evaluation uses only 8 views (16-view in appendix); primarily indoor/object-centric datasets with limited complex outdoor evaluation; SplatFormer comparison somewhat limited by different training setup; sparse-view optimization literature not fully contextualized
No adaptive iteration strategy explored: While inference supports variable iterations, no principled method for selecting iteration count at test time for dynamic speed-quality trade-offs
